correctness.rationale: For every integer n≥3, P_n is the injective incidence image of the ℓ1 unit ball. All critical exact Euclidean projection claims are proved with explicit rational feasible vectors and full necessary/sufficient subgradient inequalities for the strictly convex quadratic objective; short roots have uniform feasible upper bounds. The strict separation-four second-shell exception follows from an explicit 1/3 versus 1/4 KKT violation. Convexity and antipodal scaling prove only the endpoint roots are farthest in the whole Q_n. The standalone checker independently checks all rational certificates for 10,659 pairs through n=40 and uses independent SLSQP quadratic programs on 38 cases, maximum squared-value discrepancy 2.51e−14. Finite tests are corroborative, not a substitute for the arbitrary-n proof.

value.rationale: The problem compares two natural, widely studied symmetric edge polytopes in the same inherited Euclidean embedding; missing root directions become increasingly numerous as n grows. Exact constant Hausdorff loss from n=6 onward, unique deep holes, three sharp endpoint-sensitive distance shells, and a sharp second vertex gap give a nontrivial structural invariant of the family, of potential use for deterministic graph-root polytope approximations. This is an infinite natural classification, not a routine reformulation, arbitrary slice, or finite table.
